description: Compare each channel's average fee rate to the overall average fee rate across all linked fee records.

b.request: Among fee records linked to orders via fees.orderslink = orders.recordvault (ignoring null feerate), find the order channels (orders.orderbase) whose average feerate exceeds the overall average feerate across all linked fee records, then return one row with the mean of those channels' average feerates and the mean of their differences above the overall average, unrounded
b.sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT o.orderbase AS channel, f.feerate AS feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(feerate) AS overall_avg FROM linked), chan AS (SELECT channel, AVG(feerate) AS channel_avg FROM linked GROUP BY channel) SELECT AVG(c.channel_avg) AS mean_channel_avg_feerate, AVG(c.channel_avg - ov.overall_avg) AS mean_diff_above_overall FROM chan c CROSS JOIN overall ov WHERE c.channel_avg > ov.overall_avg

c.request: For fees tied to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), which order channels (`orders.orderbase`) have an above-average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values)? Give me one row: those channels' mean average fee rate and, on average, how far above average they are, unrounded. Compare each channel's average fee rate to the overall average fee rate across all linked fee records.
c.sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT o.orderbase, f.feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(feerate) AS overall_avg FROM linked), ch AS (SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) AS ch_avg FROM linked GROUP BY orderbase) SELECT AVG(ch.ch_avg) AS mean_avg_fee_rate, AVG(ch.ch_avg - overall.overall_avg) AS mean_excess_over_overall FROM ch, overall WHERE ch.ch_avg > overall.overall_avg

a.request: Looking at fees linked to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), compute each order channel's (`orders.orderbase`) average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values), and use the average fee rate over all those linked fee records as the benchmark. For the channels whose average is strictly above that benchmark, return a single row with the mean of their average fee rates and the mean of how far each one exceeds the benchmark, unrounded.
a.sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT o.orderbase, f.feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault), bench AS (SELECT AVG(feerate) AS b FROM linked), ch AS (SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) AS avg_rate FROM linked GROUP BY orderbase) SELECT AVG(ch.avg_rate) AS mean_avg_fee_rate, AVG(ch.avg_rate - bench.b) AS mean_excess FROM ch CROSS JOIN bench WHERE ch.avg_rate > bench.b

d.request: For fees tied to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`), compare each order channel's (`orders.orderbase`) average fee rate (`feerate`, ignoring missing values) to the overall average fee rate across all linked fee records. For the channels whose average is above the overall average, give one row with the mean of those channels' average fee rates and, on average, how far above the overall average they are, unrounded.
d.sql: WITH linked AS (SELECT o.orderbase, f.feerate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate IS NOT NULL), overall AS (SELECT AVG(feerate) AS overall_avg FROM linked), ch AS (SELECT orderbase, AVG(feerate) AS ch_avg FROM linked GROUP BY orderbase) SELECT AVG(ch.ch_avg) AS mean_channel_avg_fee_rate, AVG(ch.ch_avg - overall.overall_avg) AS mean_excess_over_overall FROM ch CROSS JOIN overall WHERE ch.ch_avg > overall.overall_avg
